title: Open extension preserves bounded-target internal-Hom continuity
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary uncompleted category $D(B_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $v:V\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with $T$ topologically Noetherian (descending chains of closed subsets stabilize). All sites and indexing categories are small in the fixed module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Filtered colimits below are termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex representatives, and all comparison maps are induced by the original cocone. For $A\in D(B_T)$ say $P_T(A)$ if (i) for every small filtered diagram $(N_i)$ of complexes with a common cohomological lower bound $c$, the evaluation-induced map $\varinjlim_i R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,N_i)\to R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,\varinjlim_iN_i)$ is an isomorphism, and (ii) there is an integer $d_A$, independent of $N,c$, such that $R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,N)\in D^{\ge c+d_A}$ whenever $N\in D^{\ge c}$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. If $P_V(A)$ holds with a chosen bound $d_A$, then $P_T(v_!A)$ holds with the same bound, where $v_!$ is exact module extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. The comparison for $v_!A$ is the evaluation-induced comparison; no constructibility assumption on $A$ is required.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(2) and Lemma 6.8.12: agent internal-sheaf, filtered-colimit refinement of open-extension stability.

proof.text: An open immersion identifies V with a subspace of the Noetherian space T, so V is Noetherian and every subset of V is compact. Hence v is quasi-compact; its monomorphism makes it separated and therefore quasi-separated. The vanishing ideal of the closed complement of the image of v gives a complementary closed immersion for the existing open/closed Hom formula.

proof.text: The categories of internal modules on V and T are Grothendieck abelian. Their filtered colimits are exact. Homology therefore preserves the termwise colimits. Naturality of colimit.post gives the square comparing colimits of natural transformations with their values on the colimit. Applying this square in every homology degree proves that a colimit of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the canonical supportPullback R from the open Hom formula. Its exactness and its adjunction with lowerStar imply that R preserves all colimits, and that its termwise complex functor preserves the chosen filtered colimits. Exact derived pullback preserves each cohomological lower bound. The natural mapDerivedCategoryFactors compares localization after termwise pullback with derived pullback after localization.

proof.text: Derived pushforward preserves every lower bound: put a bounded-below input in DerivedCategory.Plus, use negative vanishing there, and transport along rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. This is a direct application of existing bounded-below derived functor declarations, avoiding a new choice of a bounded injective resolution.

proof.text: Fix A. Represent the functor RHom(A,-) on complexes by the actual functorial K-injective replacement followed by CochainComplex.internalHom from the complex underlying Qh.objPreimage A. The existing derived closed structure defines RHom(A,-) as internalHomQhObj from exactly this representative. This identifies its right-derived functor without choosing another adjunction. The natural replacement quasi-isomorphism, invertibility of the right-derived unit at K-injectives, and the homotopy-category internal Hom comparison construct the model isomorphism explicitly.

proof.text: For N in degrees at least c, exact R takes N into degrees at least c. Apply the assumed bound to RHom(A,RN); step 4 puts its derived pushforward in degrees at least c+d. The open internal-Hom isomorphism from the complementary pair in step 1 identifies this object with RHom(v_!A,N), proving the required bound with exactly d.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1) and the open-immersion case in the proof of (2); explicit complex-model implementation by B8

proof.text: For a filtered diagram N_i with common lower bound c, the hypothesis gives invertibility of every homology-colimit comparison after termwise pullback. Preservation of colimits by R and mapDerivedCategoryFactors transfer this to RHom(A,R-). Under the natural model isomorphism of step 5, homology preservation of exact filtered colimits shows that colimit.post for the complex model is a quasi-isomorphism. Each modeled object has lower bound c+d by the other hypothesis. Apply qcqs pushforward continuity to this complex diagram. Its good-truncation comparison agrees with colimit.post followed by the image of the colimit of the truncation maps; that last map is a quasi-isomorphism by step 2. Cancel it to obtain the ordinary termwise comparison. Finally the identity colimit.post_post combines this comparison with the image of the model quasi-isomorphism, giving continuity for the composite Rv_* RHom(A,v^*(-)).

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1) and the open-immersion case in the proof of (2); explicit complex-model implementation by B8

proof.text: Fixing A in the full naturality equation of the open internal-Hom formula gives a natural isomorphism RHom(v_!A,-) ≅ Rv_* RHom(A,v^*(-)). Whisker it by localization and each homology functor. Naturality of colimit.post transports invertibility from step 7 to the exact comparison in the theorem. Every equation follows by precomposing with the original colimit inclusions; thus no arbitrary isomorphism or derived-category colimit replaces the specified comparison.
